svg.text: One ldmatrix.x4: four 8 × 8 tiles from shared memory, handed out to the warp's 32 lanes
1. In shared memory: the block's K tile
64 keys × 64 head dims; one 16 × 16 piece = four 8 × 8 tiles
16 × 16 is what a pair of multiplies needs from K
(each takes 8 keys × 16 head dims). One instruction
reads all four tiles; each value is 16 bits (bf16).
2. Tile 0, zoomed: which lane receives each value
row r goes to quad r (lanes 4r to 4r + 3), 2 values each
64 values ÷ 32 lanes = 2 values per lane per tile.
Every other lane gets its own
After one instruction, every lane holds exactly the values the multiply (MMA) wants from it, with no extra shuffling.
ldmatrix.trans does the same with each tile's rows and columns swapped, which is what V needs.
